subject: wheel bug
title: This Bug Has a Gear on Its Back, and It Melts Its Prey From the Inside

scenes.text: This bug wears a gear on its back. The gear isn't the scary part.
It's the wheel bug, an inch and a half long, with a toothed crest like half a cogwheel.
It creeps up on caterpillars and beetles, and stabs them with a beak folded under its head.
Its saliva paralyses the prey, then starts digesting it from the inside.
Then it sucks out the liquid, and leaves an empty shell.
Pick one up, and its bite hurts worse than a hornet sting. The wound can stay numb for days.

description:
The wheel bug is an assassin bug with a crest that looks like half a cogwheel.
Its saliva paralyses insects and digests them from the inside, and extension entomologists warn its bite is as bad as or worse than a hornet sting, with numbness that can last days.
Would you have touched it?
first_comment: Gardeners actually like them: they eat a lot of pests. Would you leave one on your tomatoes?
